title: Little Office of S. Dismas, the Penitent Thief, Patron of the Dying and Those in Sudden Danger of Death
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: Disma poenitens praeclare, Recolli non dedignare Oda hac canonica, Cui post seram poenitere Primo tamen patuere Paradisi ostia.
blocks.english: Illustrious penitent Dismas, disdain not [printed Recolli: unresolved infinitive] by this canonical ode, thou to whom, [printed post seram poenitere: unresolved construction], the gates of Paradise nevertheless opened first.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Recolli and post seram poenitere remain unresolved. Original English/provenance archived; printed Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Illustrious penitent Dismas, disdain not to be honoured by this canonical ode, thou to whom, after late repentance, the gates of Paradise nevertheless opened first.

blocks.source: Ant. In domo Patris mei multae sunt mansiones: erunt novissimi primi, et primi erunt novissimi.
blocks.english: Ant. In My Father’s house are many dwellings; the last shall be first, and the first shall be last.

blocks.source: ℣. In quacunque die conversus fuerit ab impietate sua
blocks.english: ℣. On whatever day he turns from his impiety,
℟. The impiety of the wicked man shall not harm him.
℣. O Dismas, be mindful of all
℟. Who are struggling with death.
℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.
Hymn

blocks.source: Non Aegyptus thura dabat Tot Idolis: abundabat Saevis quot latronibus; Inter quales et fuisse, Disma! datur, te legisse, Huc dum fugit Jesulus.
blocks.english: Egypt did not offer incense to so many idols as the fierce robbers with which it abounded. Dismas, it is granted to have read that thou also wast among them when the little Jesus fled there.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Tot ... quot is the printed comparison; datur legisse governs te fuisse. The devotional narrative is translated as printed, without independently certifying its historical claim. Original English/provenance archived; printed Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Egypt did not offer incense to so many idols as the fierce robbers with which it abounded. Dismas, it is given us to read that thou also wast among them when the little Jesus fled there.

blocks.source: Ant. Dispendentur a facie ejus idola Aegypti: lappa et tribulus ascendet super aras eorum.
blocks.english: Ant. The idols of Egypt shall be spread out before His face; burdock and thistle shall grow over their altars.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Dispendentur is the future passive of the attested rare dispendo variant of dispando (spread out), not an unprinted dispellentur or invented scattering verb. Lewis and Short, dispando/dispendo: https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn%3Acite2%3Ascaife-viewer%3Adictionary-entries.atlas_v1%3Alat.ls.perseus-eng2-n14284/ Original English/provenance archived; printed Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Ant. The idols of Egypt shall be scattered before His face; burdock and thistle shall grow over their altars.

blocks.english: ℣. He lights lamps for them,
℟. Lest they be plundered by robbers.
Let us pray,

blocks.source: Misericordissime Jesu, qui pendens in Cruce, ineffabile infinitae misericordiae tuae specimen in conversione sancti Dismas latronis ostendisti: per sanguinem tuum pretiosum in Cruce effusum, obsecro te, concede mihi ingratissimo peccatori efficacem tuam gratiam, ut peccata mea deplorare, te toto corde amare, et in hora mortis meae audire a te merear: Hodie mecum eris in Paradiso. Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre etc.
blocks.english: Most merciful Jesus, Who, hanging upon the Cross, didst show an ineffable example of Thine infinite mercy in the conversion of Saint Dismas the thief: through Thy precious Blood shed upon the Cross, I beseech Thee, grant me, a most ungrateful sinner, Thy efficacious grace, that I may bewail my sins, love Thee with my whole heart, and deserve to hear from Thee at the hour of my death, “Today thou shalt be with Me in Paradise.” Who livest and reignest with God the Father, etc.
℣. O Dismas, be mindful of all
℟. Who are struggling with death.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.
Hymn

blocks.source: Dum sub palma Joseph pater Sedet, atque nato mater Jesulo advigilat, Tu cum assectis prorumpis, Supplex vero mox procumbis, Pupus te dum advocat.
blocks.english: While Joseph the father sits beneath the palm, and the mother watches over the little Jesus her Son, thou dost rush forth with thy followers, but soon fall down in supplication when the Child calls thee.

blocks.source: Ant. Quare posuisti me contrarium tibi, et arbitratus es me inimicum tuum?
blocks.english: Ant. Why hast Thou set me against Thee, and accounted me Thine enemy?

blocks.source: ℣. Ego cum exaltatus fuero de terra,
blocks.english: ℣. When I am lifted up from the earth,
℟. I shall draw all things to Myself.
Prayer as above.

blocks.source: Quin jam sociis relictis, Hospitem te das afflictis, Ducem et itineris; At non diu! nam reversus Ad sodales, mox immersus Priscis es flagitiis.
blocks.english: Indeed, leaving thy companions, thou now dost offer thyself as host to the afflicted and guide for their journey. But not for long! Returning to thy fellows, thou art soon immersed in thine old crimes.

blocks.source: Ant. Odisti disciplinam, et projecisti sermones meos retrorsum: cum videbas furem, currebas cum eo.
blocks.english: Ant. Thou didst hate discipline and cast My words behind thee; when thou sawest a thief, thou didst run with him.
℣. With the chosen thou shalt be chosen,
℟. And with the perverse thou shalt be perverted.
Prayer as above.

blocks.source: En! jam Christus, instar Ducis, Per virtutes viam Crucis Intrat et miracula, Num et tu ad Crucem perges? Imo certe! sed huc verges Probra per et scelera.
blocks.english: Behold, now Christ, as a leader, enters the way of the Cross through virtues and miracles. Wilt thou also go to the Cross? Indeed, certainly! But thou wilt turn there through disgrace and crimes.

blocks.source: Ant. Fecit oriri solem suum super bonos et malos, et pluit super justos et injustos.
blocks.english: Ant. He made His sun rise upon the good and the evil, and rains upon the just and the unjust.

blocks.source: ℣. Justum autem deducet Dominus per vias rectas,
blocks.english: ℣. But the Lord shall lead the just through straight paths,
℟. And the wicked shall walk in a circle.
Prayer as above.

blocks.source: At, quam multum obliquabas Iter Dismae, et distabas Recta Christi semita, Tamen hi, per pares mortes, Viae sancti sunt consortes Rursum in Calvaria.
blocks.english: Yet how greatly thou didst bend Dismas’s way aside and depart from Christ’s straight path! Nevertheless these, through like deaths, are holy companions of the way again on Calvary.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Dismae is genitive modifying Iter; sancti is nominative plural with hi/consortes, and Viae genitive of the way. Neither requires a changed case or an unprinted adjective sanctae. Original English/provenance archived; printed Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Yet how greatly, Dismas, thou didst bend thy way aside and depart from Christ’s straight path! Nevertheless, through like deaths, [the defective printed clause concerning companions on the holy way is unresolved] again on Calvary.

blocks.source: Ant. Pro eo enim, quod tradidit in mortem animam suam, et peccata multorum tulit, cum sceleratis reputatus est.
blocks.english: Ant. For because He surrendered His soul to death and bore the sins of many, He was numbered with the wicked.

blocks.source: ℣. Ducebantur autem et alii duo nequam cum eo,
blocks.english: ℣. And two other criminals were led with Him,
℟. To be put to death.
Prayer as above.

blocks.source: Disma, quae haec paradoxa? Par est poena, dispar noxa, Tu sons, Christus innocens: Porro nec vercundaris, Sons insolens, criminari, Probrum terrae, summum Ens.
blocks.english: Dismas, what paradox is this? Equal punishment, unequal guilt: thou art guilty, Christ innocent. Yet thou art not [printed vercundaris: unresolved verb], insolent in thy guilt, a disgrace to the earth, to accuse the Supreme Being.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. The printed vercundaris is not silently replaced by verecundaris. Original English/provenance archived; printed Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Dismas, what paradox is this? Equal punishment, unequal guilt: thou art guilty, Christ innocent. Yet thou art not ashamed, insolent in thy guilt, a disgrace to the earth, to accuse the Supreme Being.

blocks.source: Ant. Nequitiam et iniquitatem in excelso locuti sunt: posuerunt in coelum os suum.
blocks.english: Ant. They spoke wickedness and iniquity from on high; they set their mouths against heaven.

blocks.source: ℣. Si tu es Christus, salvum fac temetipsum et nos,
blocks.english: ℣. If Thou art Christ, save Thyself and us.

blocks.source: ℟. Alios salvos facis, te ipsum non potes salvum facere.
blocks.english: ℟. Thou savest others; Thou canst not save Thyself.
Prayer as above.

blocks.source: Unus Christi sed aspectus Sic contudit tibi pectus Alta missus arbore, Mox ut totus indoleres, Caedes, spolia defleres, Noxas et blasphemiae.
blocks.english: But one glance of Christ, sent from the lofty tree, so smote thy breast that at once thou wast wholly filled with sorrow, bewailing murders, plunder, and the offences of blasphemy.

blocks.source: Ant. Exaudi me Domine, quoniam benigna est misericordia tua: secundum multitudinem miserationum tuarum respice in me.
blocks.english: Ant. Hear me, Lord, for Thy mercy is good; according to the multitude of Thy mercies look upon me.

blocks.source: ℣. Et nos quidem digna factis recipimus,
blocks.english: ℣. And we indeed receive what our deeds deserve,
℟. But this Man has done no evil.
Prayer as above.

blocks.english: ℣. O Dismas, be mindful of all
℟. Who are struggling with death.
℣. [Printed Convertere nos: unresolved construction], O God our Saviour.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Convertere nos is not the customary active imperative Converte nos; no unprinted ending supplied. Original English/provenance archived; printed Latin unchanged.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.
℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.
Hymn

blocks.source: Venia sic impetrata, Dismae Paradisi grata Jam et regna exspectat; Cui et Jesus prompto ore, Hodie se adhuc fore Ibi secum, innuit.
blocks.english: Pardon thus obtained, he now also awaits the realms of Paradise pleasing to Dismas; and Jesus readily indicates to him that this very day he shall be there with Him.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Dismae is dative with grata, which agrees with accusative plural regna. Exspectat has an implicit subject; there is no defective agreement requiring a nominative Disma. The reported personal references retain the narrative’s Dismas/Jesus relation. Original English/provenance archived; printed Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Having thus obtained pardon, Dismas now awaits the pleasant realms of Paradise; and Jesus readily tells him that this very day he shall be there with Him.

blocks.source: Ant. Apud Dominum propitiatio est, et copiosa apud eum redemptio: et ipse redimet Israel ex omnibus iniquitatibus ejus.
blocks.english: Ant. With the Lord there is forgiveness, and with Him plentiful redemption; and He shall redeem Israel from all his iniquities.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine, memento mei, cum veneris in regnum tuum.
blocks.english: ℣. Lord, remember me when Thou comest into Thy kingdom.

blocks.source: ℟. Amen. dico tibi: hodie mecum eris in Paradiso.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen, I say to thee: today thou shalt be with Me in Paradise.
Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed direction repeats this office’s own Matins collect.

blocks.source: Disma, fac et nos sincero, Sed dolore non tam sero Portum coeli tangere; Quodsi vero id sit sero, Luctu fac hoc plus severo Culpas nostras plangere.
blocks.english: Dismas, grant that we also may reach the harbour of heaven with sincere sorrow, yet not so late. But if it should indeed be late, grant that we may bewail our faults with all the deeper mourning.

blocks.source: Ant. Suavis Dominus universis, patiens et multum misericors: et miserationes ejus super omnia opera ejus.
blocks.english: Ant. The Lord is gracious to all, patient and very merciful; and His mercies are over all His works.
℣. A sacrifice to God is an afflicted spirit;

blocks.source: ℟. Cor contritum et humiliatum Deus non despicies.
blocks.english: ℟. A contrite and humbled heart, O God, Thou wilt not despise.
℣. Pray for us, blessed Dismas.
℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.
Prayer

blocks.source: Sancte Disma, qui mira Dei providentia ex nefario latrone in eximium poenitentiae speculum evasisti, et paucas intra horas aeterna tibi gaudia comparasti: dignare de excelso gloriae tuae throno, sicut in te de Cruce aspexit Christus, super miseriam hanc lachrymarum vallem oculos tuos defigere; et quoniam tibi cognita est mentis humanae fragilitas, semper ad malum magis, quam ad bonum proclivis; igitur nobis, apud dulcissimum Redemptorem nostrum, precibus tuis impetra, ut sicut per gratiam suam efficacem ad poenitentiam et Paradisi coelestis gloriam te perduxit, ita et nos famulos suos eadem efficaci gratia ad dignos poenitentiae fructus impellat, quo commissis nostris corditus deploratis, pie quondam tibi commoremur, ac una tandem in Deo Salvatori nostro jugiter exultemus, qui vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Saint Dismas, who by the wonderful providence of God didst become, from a wicked robber, an outstanding example of repentance, and within a few hours didst obtain eternal joys for thyself: deign from the lofty throne of thy glory to fix thine eyes upon this misery, this valley of tears, as Christ looked upon thee from the Cross. And since thou knowest the frailty of the human mind, always more inclined to evil than to good, obtain for us by thy prayers before our sweetest Redeemer that, as He led thee by His efficacious grace to repentance and the glory of heavenly Paradise, so He may urge us His servants by that same efficacious grace to worthy fruits of repentance; that, having [printed corditus: unresolved adverb] bewailed our offences, we may one day dwell devoutly with thee, and at last together rejoice continually [printed in Deo Salvatori nostro: unresolved case connection], Who liveth and reigneth for ever and ever. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Corditus and in Deo Salvatori nostro remain unresolved; no repaired case ending supplied. Original English/provenance archived; printed Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Saint Dismas, who by the wonderful providence of God didst become, from a wicked robber, an outstanding example of repentance, and within a few hours didst obtain eternal joys for thyself: deign from the lofty throne of thy glory to fix thine eyes upon this misery, this valley of tears, as Christ looked upon thee from the Cross. And since thou knowest the frailty of the human mind, always more inclined to evil than to good, obtain for us by thy prayers before our sweetest Redeemer that, as He led thee by His efficacious grace to repentance and the glory of heavenly Paradise, so He may urge us His servants by that same efficacious grace to worthy fruits of repentance; that, having heartily bewailed our offences, we may one day dwell devoutly with thee, and at last together rejoice continually in God our Saviour, Who liveth and reigneth for ever and ever. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: Prepared English was compared visually with PDF pages 476–479. All eight printed hours, the ingressus, and the commendation remain. Repeated collect directions expand from this office’s Matins. The hymn’s devotional narrative is translated as printed; defective Latin remains visibly provisional or unresolved, keeping source reading pending.

10 October 2026: all four rendered PDF pages and all 97 passages personally compared, including Sulamittis Officiosa (1714) attribution, Ingressus, seven hours, Commendation, seven same-office collect expansions and continuations. Four pending passages resolved without changing Latin: printed historical narrative, attested rare Dispendentur, genitive Iter Dismae/nominative sancti, and dative Dismae with grata regna. Convertere nos returned to pending. Four source blockers explicitly bracketed; original English/provenance archived.
